chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
He who gallops with the rein of his desire will stumble at his appointed time.

key_terms.أَجَل: Appointed time; lifespan or time of death
key_terms.عِنَان: Rein; a metaphor for control or restraint

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to 'gallop with the rein of desire' in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: In this aphorism from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) illustrates the causal link between unbridled self-indulgence (hawa) and the hastening of death, a concept deeply rooted in Shia ethical theology where the soul's lack of discipline accelerates its decay. This teaching serves as a practical reminder for believers to exercise self-restraint (muraqabah) to preserve their lifespan and spiritual vitality, contrasting with the impulsive actions that lead to premature demise.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 19. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
He who gallops with loose rein collides with death.
